name: Draw simple cartoons
blurb: Cartooning is about simplification and exaggeration, not accuracy — which makes it far more achievable than realism and much faster to get good at.
gear: A sketchbook and a fineliner or brush pen
steps: Learn to build figures from basic shapes: circles, ovals and simple lines for the skeleton.
Learn expression from a small set of variables — eyebrow angle, eye size, mouth curve — and draw a sheet of 20 expressions.
Learn the line of action: one sweeping curve through the whole figure that gives it energy before any detail.
Develop a repeatable character you can draw from any angle, which is much harder and more valuable than one good drawing.
Learn to exaggerate: find the one feature that defines a subject and push it well past reality.
Draw one small cartoon a day for a month, finished and inked.
tips: Consistency beats polish. A character that looks the same across ten drawings reads as a character.
Simplify aggressively. Every removed line makes the drawing read faster.
proof: You draw your own character from four angles with three different expressions, recognisably the same person.
